text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd said on Monday its regional carrier Silkair plans to purchase about 12 aircraft to expand its fleet.
The airline was trying to decide whether to buy the planes from Europe's Airbus Industries or America's Boeing, an airline spokeswoman said.
But she declined to say what the deal would be worth as negotiations were still going on.

A report in Singapore's daily Business Times on Monday quoted Silkair general manager Michael Chan as saying: "We are currently evaluating the proposals from the two manufacturers and will make the final decision by the end of April."
Silkair, which currently flies to 22 destinations, wants the first aircraft to be delivered by the second half of next year. It currently has six Boeing 737-300s and two Fokker 70s.
Chan said Silkair plans to buy aircraft from a single family in the future, either Airbus or Boeing, with the latter having an edge because of its greater variety, the Business Times reported.
